entries.title: Advocacy notify dialog lets you email only new campaign recipients
entries.summary: When sending notifications on a campaign that has already been emailed, the **Notify** dialog now offers two choices: **Everyone (N)** to re-send to all recipients, or **Only new (M)** to reach only people added since the last send. The counts come from a live dry run so you always know exactly how many people will receive the message before you confirm.
entries.use_case: Campaigns that grow over time — such as rolling attendee invitations — previously required organizers to manually track who had already been notified to avoid duplicate emails. The **Only new** option lets organizers safely re-open the notify dialog at any point and send only to people who haven't received the campaign email yet.

cs_action.note: Requires the companion API change in lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4584. Until that API ships, the dry-run call returns a 400, the Only new option stays hidden, and Notify behaves as before — no customer impact during the gap.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a rolling Advocacy campaign asks how to avoid re-emailing people who already received a campaign notification.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Advocacy campaigns where recipients are added in batches over time.
internal.gotchas: The Only new option is hidden until the API (web-api#4584) is deployed. Deploy order is safe — no regression if the UI ships first.
internal.talk_track: Once your campaign has been sent, the Notify dialog will show you two options: resend to everyone, or reach only the people added since your last send — with exact counts so you know what you're about to do.

entries.title: Disclosures: seven reliability fixes across requests, forms, embeds and the master switch
entries.summary: Seven bugs in the Disclosures workflow are resolved: turning the **Disclosures** master switch off now silences the obligations badge on Contacts; whitespace-only mitigation notes are rejected; blank or whitespace form names are rejected with a clear error; submitting a disclosure now closes every other open request for that contact (staff Record, CFP inline, portal, magic link); the speakers embed and gallery widgets now include the disclosure opt-in slot alongside the agenda embed; a form snapshot is saved at send time so editing the live form after sending does not change the link already delivered to the contact; and a malformed token in a public disclosure link now returns a clean 404 instead of a regex error.
entries.use_case: Organizers running CME or accredited events rely on Disclosures being accurate and consistent. These fixes ensure the badge, open requests, form versions, and embed data all reflect the true state of each contact's disclosure without manual cleanup.

cs_action.note: Seven distinct fixes ship together. Verify on a live event: (1) toggle Disclosures off → Contacts badge goes quiet; (2) Record action clears the open request; (3) send a request, edit the form, open the link — recipient sees the sent version; (4) speakers.json shows disclosure slot when show_in_embeds is on.

internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Disclosures beta, especially those running accredited or CME events.
internal.staff_path: Org → Contacts → [contact] → Disclosures tab; Event → Embeds → speakers.json
internal.gotchas: The form-snapshot migration (20261021130000) adds a JSONB column; existing requests without a snapshot fall back to the live form — only newly sent requests capture a snapshot. Amounts are never exposed in the embed slot, only entity and nature.
internal.talk_track: Disclosures now locks in the exact form version you sent, so editing your form later won't confuse speakers who already received a link. And when a speaker submits, every other open request for them closes automatically — no more chasing duplicates.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a note that the form version is frozen at send time (form snapshot), that submitting one request closes all other pending requests for the same contact, and that the speakers embed now includes the disclosure opt-in slot when show_in_embeds is enabled.
draft.why_use_it: Disclosures lets you collect, track and manage conflict-of-interest declarations from speakers and other participants directly inside Sessionboard. You can send requests, set automatic reminders, record mitigations, and export the results for your accreditor — all linked to the contact record so nothing falls through the cracks.

entries.title: Disclosures: five UI fixes for the security widget, invalid links, Mitigations tab, contact sidebar errors, and column filter label
entries.summary: Five bugs in the Disclosures flow are resolved: (1) The Turnstile security widget on the public disclosure page now shows a **Retry** button when it fails to load instead of staying blank. (2) A truncated or malformed disclosure link now immediately shows "This link isn't valid" without making an unnecessary API call. entries.title: Slides: multiple fixes to generate, attach, jobs, templates, and session file badges
entries.summary: A sweep of fixes across the Slides feature: double-clicking **Generate slides**, **Attach to sessions**, **Add to presentations**, or **Regenerate** no longer creates duplicate jobs. The **Jobs** tab now shows **Showing N of total** with a **Load more** button when there are more than the first page of results. The **All sessions** scope hint now reads "Every session on the Sessions list. Drafts (unsubmitted submissions) are left out." Navigating back through the generate wizard no longer replaces picked session names with raw IDs. A deleted or invalid template no longer hangs on "Loading template…" — the designer shows "This template no longer exists" with a **Back to templates** link. After a successful **Attach**, the dialog no longer shows a false "no finished sessions" state. Password-protected PDFs now show the skip reason "This PDF is password-protected. Remove the password and upload it again." **Add to presentations** now excludes title slides and merged copies from the count, and defaults to the job's template rather than the first available. The **Regenerate** toast now reports how many files could not be updated and names them. The session **Files** tab now shows **Merged copy** and **Out of date** badges on "-with-title-slide" copies, each with their own **Regenerate** button. Presentations & files checkboxes and pagination controls now have accessible labels for screen readers. **Bulk Create** in the Sessions list is no longer incorrectly disabled when only the Title column is visible.
entries.use_case: Events that generate title slides at scale were hitting silent failures — duplicate jobs, stale dialogs, missing badges on merged copies, and misleading success toasts. These fixes make the generate-attach-merge workflow reliable enough to use without manual verification after each step.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports duplicate slide jobs, stale attach dialogs, missing out-of-date badges on merged copies, or confusing regenerate toasts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively using Slides to generate or merge title slides.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Slides → Jobs tab / session Files tab
internal.gotchas: The jobs paging (Load more) and the 4xx retry fix both require the companion API PR #4593 to be deployed; the UI changes are safe before that deploy but full behaviour requires both halves.
internal.talk_track: We fixed a batch of rough edges in Slides: double-clicking no longer fires duplicate jobs, the Jobs tab now pages through all results, merged copies show their own Out of date badge with a Regenerate button, and the Regenerate toast tells you exactly which files failed.

draft.docs_gap: The Slides guide should document the new "Showing N of total · Load more" pagination on the Jobs tab, the "This template no longer exists" error state in the template designer, the per-copy Merged copy / Out of date badge on the session Files tab, and the updated "All sessions" scope description.
draft.why_use_it: Slides lets you generate branded title slides for every session and attach or merge them into speaker-uploaded presentations automatically. Use it to produce a consistent look across hundreds of sessions without touching each file by hand, and to keep merged copies up to date whenever session details change.

entries.title: Multiple Slides and title-slide fixes: draft sessions excluded, broken headshots show initials, encrypted PDFs rejected, contrast improved, and more
entries.summary: A sweep of twelve bugs in the **Slides** title-slide feature. Key fixes: draft sessions are no longer included in **All sessions** generated slide runs; speaker headshots that cannot be fetched now show the speaker's initials disc instead of a blank circle; password-protected PDFs are rejected at merge time with a clear error instead of producing blank title pages; organizer-generated copies are no longer stacked as a second title slide when merging; text contrast on mid-tone brand colour bands now meets the 4.5:1 minimum; template names with special characters (e.g. `R&D`) are stored and displayed correctly; and the **Jobs** list supports paging so events with many runs can browse all of them.
entries.use_case: Events that generate title slides for all sessions were silently including draft sessions that are hidden everywhere else in the product. Organizers can now trust that a full-event slide run matches exactly the sessions visible in the Sessions list, and that merged presentations will not stack duplicate title slides or produce blank pages from encrypted PDFs.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their generated slide deck included sessions they had not published yet, that a merged presentation had two title slides, that a speaker's headshot showed as a blank circle, or that a password-protected PDF caused a silent merge failure.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively using the Slides title-slide generation and merge feature.
internal.gotchas: One live template in US had an HTML-entity-encoded name (e.g. &amp;). An optional SQL cleanup script is in the PR body — coordinate with engineering if a customer reports garbled template names. The jobs list now pages (offset/limit) so customers with many runs will see a total count and can navigate beyond the first 50.
internal.talk_track: We fixed a batch of edge cases in Slides: draft sessions stay out of generated runs, broken or untrusted headshot URLs fall back to the speaker's initials, encrypted PDFs are flagged instead of silently producing blank pages, and duplicate title slides no longer stack when you re-merge. Text on mid-tone brand colours also now meets accessibility contrast requirements.

draft.docs_gap: The Slides guide should document: (1) that draft sessions are excluded from All Sessions runs; (2) that headshots falling back to initials when the image cannot be fetched; (3) that password-protected PDFs are rejected at merge time with an "encrypted" reason; (4) that the Jobs list is paginated; and (5) the 4.5:1 contrast requirement for brand colour bands.
draft.why_use_it: Slides lets you generate branded title slides for every session and merge them into uploaded speaker presentations automatically. It saves the production team hours of manual file work and keeps every deck on-brand without touching individual files. Use it when you need a consistent look across dozens or hundreds of session recordings or live-stream files.

entries.title: Sessionboard e-sign: signed-copy download, sender message, inline PDF viewer, and a sweep of signing-flow fixes
entries.summary: A batch of fixes and additions to the Sessionboard native e-sign flow. Signers now receive a **Download signed copy** button in their completion email that streams the signed PDF via a secure, token-gated link. The sender's custom message (with merge variables resolved) appears on the signing page and in invite, your-turn, and reminder emails, using the custom subject line. An inline unsigned-PDF viewer is available on the `/sign/:token` page. Additional fixes: voiding a contract is blocked once it is completed, declined, or executed; submitting field values for another signer's fields returns a clear error; templates whose module does not match the subject (e.g. a Groups template sent to a contact) are refused at send time; duplicate template names return a 409 instead of a 500; typed-signature SVGs now scale to fit long names and emoji; uploaded PDFs are validated for the `%PDF-` header and date-range rules; error messages for bad or expired signing tokens are now consistent 404s; the sponsor signer is no longer guessed from an arbitrary account contact and stays editable when no primary contact is set; **Add Contract** ignores double clicks, accepts only PDFs and checks dates; and the signing page keeps the signer's chosen language and wraps its toolbar on phones.
entries.use_case: Organizers using Sessionboard e-sign can now trust that signers receive a working download link for their signed copy, see the sender's personalised message throughout the flow, and encounter clear, consistent errors if something goes wrong — reducing support requests around lost copies and confusing error pages.

cs_action.note: Two database migrations ship with this PR (copy-token column + email template text update). Verify both have run on US and EU before directing customers to the new download-copy link or the inline viewer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why signers can't download their signed copy, or reports confusing error messages on the signing page, or asks about the sender message not appearing in emails.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Sessionboard native e-sign (Contracts beta).
internal.staff_path: CRM → Contracts → [contract] → Signers tab; completion email → Download signed copy
internal.gotchas: The inline unsigned-PDF viewer on /sign/:token requires the companion UI PR (sessionboard-web-ui-v2, same branch). The documents S3 bucket had no CORS, so the viewer was always broken before this fix — reassure customers this is now resolved. The copy-token is minted at finalize time, so contracts completed before this deploy will not have a download link in their old completion emails.
internal.talk_track: After a signer completes a contract, they now get a 'Download signed copy' button right in their completion email — no need to chase the organizer for a PDF. And the custom message you write when sending the contract now shows up on the signing page and in every email the signer receives, so the experience feels personal and on-brand.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document: (1) the new Download signed copy link in completion emails and the /contracting/signed-copy/:token endpoint; (2) that the sender message and custom subject appear on the signing page and in invite/reminder emails with merge variables resolved; (3) the inline unsigned-PDF viewer on the signing page; (4) validation rules for manually uploaded PDFs (PDF header check, date-range constraints); and (5) which contract statuses allow voiding.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's built-in e-sign lets you send, track, and collect legally binding signatures without leaving the platform or paying for a third-party tool. Signers complete agreements from their portal or a public signing link, and both parties receive a signed copy automatically. Use it whenever you need a fast, auditable signature on speaker agreements, sponsor contracts, or any other document tied to your event contacts.

entries.title: Daily summary emails show the real notification instead of placeholder text
entries.summary: Three kinds of line in the daily summary email used to show generic text with no link. A document-request comment now reads **[Name] commented on "[request]"** with the comment, and several comments on one request fold into one line ending **(N comments)**. A call-for-proposals close reminder reads **Finish your submission for [event]** with the form and its close date. An evaluation reminder reads **[Plan]: N reviews left** with progress and the deadline. Each line links to the page it is about. Admin summaries are sent from **Sessionboard** instead of **Sessionboard (via Sessionboard)**.

where.path: Daily summary email (Email frequency set to Daily summary)

entries.use_case: People who get one email a day can act on it straight away: who commented on what, which submission is about to close, how many reviews are left — each with a link.

internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone whose email frequency is Daily summary; no action needed.

internal.talk_track: People who get one email a day can act on it straight away: who commented on what, which submission is about to close, how many reviews are left — each with a link.

entries.title: Compare an external event's topics with one of your events in Scout
entries.summary: The **Intelligence** tab on a scouted external event now compares its topics with one of your events. Pick the event in **Compare with**, then switch between **Summary**, **Focus & convergence** and **All topics**: topics you share, **Affinity matches** you can **Unify** or **Dismiss**, **Opportunities** only the external event covers, and **Differentials** only yours covers. The **Agenda** tab gains a **Topics** column for each external session.

where.path: Organization → CRM → Scout → External Events → [event] → Intelligence

entries.use_case: Program teams can see in a minute which topics a competing or peer conference covers that theirs does not, and where the two already overlap.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer benchmarks their program against another conference or asks what topics they are missing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Speaker Prospects / Scout who crawl external events.
internal.staff_path: Organization → CRM → Scout → External Events → [event] → Intelligence
internal.gotchas: Needs web-api #4547 live; without it the comparison 404s and the Agenda shows no topic chips. Focus & convergence runs a model on the first request for a pair (about 5 s, then cached). Unify makes the topics synonyms and can only be undone from the taxonomy review.
internal.talk_track: Program teams can see in a minute which topics a competing or peer conference covers that theirs does not, and where the two already overlap.

entries.title: Ask, the AI assistant, in the signed-in Sites portal
entries.summary: Speakers, participants, reviewers, judges and awards entrants signed in to a Site can open **Ask** from a button in the bottom-right corner. It answers from their own tasks, submissions, review assignments and entries, with cards that open the right page — a task, the next unfinished review, a draft entry or its checkout. Reviewers get the rubric and guidelines but never scores, and entrants never see judges, scores or other entries. Answers can be rated or passed to the organizer where messaging allows, and someone with more than one role picks which one they are asking as.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to turn on Ask for your Site

entries.use_case: Speakers, reviewers and entrants get their "what do I still need to do?" answered on the spot, which cuts the questions your team answers by email.

cs_action.note: Ask is off by default for every Site audience (participant, evaluator, awards entrant). Staff turn it on per audience from the Assistants admin page (super users only); the organization also needs AI features on.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with a busy CFP, review cycle or awards program asks how to cut repeat questions from speakers, reviewers or entrants.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running a Sessionboard Site for speakers, reviewers or awards entrants.
internal.staff_path: Assistants admin page (super users) → Site profiles
internal.gotchas: Nothing shows until the web-api releases with #4611, #4614 and #4617 are live; the button is hidden in the Site builder preview. internal.talk_track: Speakers, reviewers and entrants get their "what do I still need to do?" answered on the spot, which cuts the questions your team answers by email.

entries.title: Stop an Ask answer while it is still being written
entries.summary: While **Ask** is writing an answer in the organizer panel, a **Stop** button takes the place of **Send**; click it to stop the answer. In voice mode, tapping to interrupt or talking over Ask stops it too. A stopped answer keeps a small **Stopped** label, also after a reload.
entries.use_case: When Ask heads off in the wrong direction you can stop it and rephrase instead of waiting for the whole answer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer finds long Ask answers slow or wants to correct a question mid-answer.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organizer using Ask; no action needed.

internal.talk_track: When Ask heads off in the wrong direction you can stop it and rephrase instead of waiting for the whole answer.

entries.title: Talk to Ask by voice in the organizer panel
entries.summary: A **Talk with Ask** button in the **Ask** panel opens voice mode: speak your question, watch the live captions and hear the answer read back sentence by sentence. One round button starts talking, sends now or interrupts, and **Escape** goes back to typing. In the US, speech is transcribed by Sessionboard's speech service. In the EU and Middle East, voice uses only the browser's on-device recognition and voices; where the browser has none, the mic is replaced by **Voice needs on-device speech recognition in this browser.**

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether Ask can be used hands-free or by voice.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organizer using Ask; no action needed.
internal.gotchas: US transcription needs web-api #4599 and #4604 live; until then the panel falls back to on-device recognition everywhere. On-device recognition is Chrome-only today, so Safari and Firefox show the note instead of the mic in the EU and ME. Answers are spoken with browser voices. Talking over Ask on laptop speakers can trigger an interrupt; tapping always works.
internal.talk_track: Organizers walking a venue or juggling a laptop can ask a question out loud and listen to the answer instead of typing.

entries.title: Reviewer portal: prior-round scores, view-only after the deadline, and a tidier review page
entries.summary: Reviewers in a later round see a sticky **Prior round** strip with each earlier round's cumulative score and a collapsible **Prior round feedback** card above the scorecard. Team leads and event administrators also get a **Reviewer breakdown** of each earlier round: every assigned reviewer's total score, shared comments, and whether they **Completed**, **Abstained**, left it **Incomplete** or **Not started**. When a round is kept visible after its deadline, **My Reviews** marks it **Closed · View only** and it opens read-only. The session builder shows full abstract titles, presenters and category; **Quick jump** is narrower and folds into a rail that shows the active-filter count; long participant lists start collapsed and scroll in their own box; and the **Messages** section only appears when messaging is on for the plan.
entries.use_case: In multi-round reviews, reviewers see last round's scores where they score, and know at a glance when scoring has closed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running multi-round reviews asks how reviewers can see prior scores, or reviewers are unsure whether scoring is still open.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans with several rounds, blind review or messaging off.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → open the reviewer portal
internal.gotchas: The prior-round blocks render only once web-api #4588 is live. In blind rounds, participant blocks that would show only a role are dropped. Most US plans (1,487 of 1,565) have messaging off, so most reviewers lose the messaging panel.
internal.talk_track: In multi-round reviews, reviewers see last round's scores where they score, and know at a glance when scoring has closed.

entries.title: Attendee Ask: answers from session transcripts, suggested actions, ratings and questions for your team
entries.summary: In the Attend app, **Ask** can now quote a session's live captions or recorded transcript, and suggest actions — add a session to My schedule (with the day's gaps and clashes), show a place on the map, request a meeting or message a team — each only when that feature is on. *Near me* questions use the attendee's latest room check-in or booth scan. The inbox has no filter for attendee questions yet, and replies cannot carry attachments.
internal.talk_track: Attendees get answers about what a speaker actually said and a one-tap next step, and the questions Ask cannot answer reach your team instead of being lost.

entries.title: Cloned events remap Attend app filters to new content, and push notifications can target custom app pages
entries.summary: When an event is cloned, the **Attend** app's list-page filters (tracks, session types, topics, levels, rooms, tiers, and hand-picked session or account IDs) are automatically remapped to the equivalent entities in the new event instead of carrying over the source event's IDs. Filters whose entities were not copied are widened to show all content rather than nothing. Separately, push notifications can now target a specific custom app page by its ID (`page:<id>`); the **Notifications** composer exposes these pages under **Custom Pages** so organizers can deep-link attendees directly to a custom page.

where.path: Attend → Notifications; Attend → App Design (on clone)

entries.use_case: Annual-event teams who clone last year's event no longer need to manually rebuild every filtered Agenda, People, or Partners page in the app — the filters point at the new event's content automatically. Teams running sponsor or exhibitor activations can also send a push notification that drops attendees directly onto a specific custom app page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer clones an annual event that uses the Attend app with filtered list pages, or when they ask about targeting push notifications to a specific custom page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend app (beta) who clone events year-over-year and/or use custom pages in their app layout.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → Notifications → New Notification → Destination → Custom Pages
internal.gotchas: Filters whose entities were not cloned (e.g. hand-picked sessions when sessions weren't copied) are widened to show all content — admins should review filtered pages after cloning. Days are not shifted; cloned sessions retain their original dates. Custom page push targets require the mobile app to route 'page:<id>' targets — confirm mobile client version supports this before promoting to customers.
internal.talk_track: If you clone your event each year, the Attend app's filtered pages now automatically point at your new tracks, rooms, and session types — no manual cleanup needed. And if you want to send a push notification that takes attendees straight to a specific custom page in your app, you can now pick that page right in the notification composer.

draft.docs_gap: The clone-an-event guide should note that Attend app list-page filters are remapped to the new event's entities on clone, and explain the widening behaviour when entities were not copied. The notifications guide should document the new Custom Pages destination option and note that the mobile app must support page-target routing.
draft.why_use_it: The Attend mobile app lets organizers curate filtered list pages — showing only certain tracks, session types, rooms, or hand-picked sessions — and send push notifications to drive attendees to specific destinations. When you clone an event for a recurring conference, the app layout carries forward with filters already mapped to the new event's content. Push notifications support deep links to built-in pages and custom pages, so a single tap takes attendees exactly where you want them.

entries.title: Read-only scoring banner shows a clearer message when a plan is closed before the round deadline

entries.title: Attend app sends smart push nudges for saved sessions and nearby places
entries.summary: Three new push notification kinds are available for the Attend mobile app — **Starts Soon** (a saved session is about to begin), **Gap Filler** (a saved session is ending and a free slot is coming up, with a suggested session), and **Nearby** (an attendee checks in or scans a booth). All three are off by default and require organizers to enable nudges and each individual kind. Attendees can opt out of nudges per device from **Me → Notifications** in the app.

enable.path: Attend → App Settings → Nudges → enable nudges and each kind

where.path: Attend → App Settings → Nudges (organizer config); Me → Notifications (attendee opt-out in the app)

entries.use_case: Events that want to drive session attendance and exhibitor engagement can automatically prompt attendees at the right moment — when a saved session is about to start, when a gap in their schedule opens up, or when they walk into a room or past a booth — without requiring organizers to manually send push notifications.

cs_action.note: All three nudge kinds (ask_starts_soon, ask_gap, ask_nearby) are off by default. Organizers must turn on nudges and each kind individually in Attend → App Settings → Nudges. The Ask feature (AI assistant) must also be on for gap-filler suggestions to work.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to increase session attendance or exhibitor booth traffic, or when they want to reduce the manual work of sending push notifications during the event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend mobile app (beta) who have Ask enabled and want automated, schedule-aware attendee engagement.
internal.gotchas: Nudges only reach attendees with a registered push token who have not opted out. The ask_gap kind requires the For You / gap_filler recommendation engine to be running. Push text intentionally omits room and booth names (lock-screen privacy); the app surfaces the name in-app via the data payload. A web-ui-v2 History label for the push.nudges_updated activity action is a follow-up and not yet visible in the admin history view.
internal.talk_track: Instead of manually sending a push blast before every session, the app can now automatically remind attendees when a session they saved is about to start, suggest something to fill a gap in their schedule, and ping them when they walk into a room or scan a booth — all with attendee opt-out built in.

draft.docs_gap: The Send push notifications guide should add a section covering the three nudge kinds (Starts Soon, Gap Filler, Nearby), how to enable each, quiet-hours configuration for nudges, the per-attendee opt-out flow in Me → Notifications, and the dedupe/cap behaviour that prevents attendees from being over-notified.
draft.why_use_it: Push nudges let the Attend app reach attendees at the moments that matter most during an event, without any manual effort from the event team. Attendees who save sessions receive timely reminders and gap-filling suggestions based on their personal schedule, while location-based nudges surface relevant content the moment someone enters a room or scans a booth. Organizers control which nudge kinds are active and can set quiet hours so attendees are never interrupted at the wrong time. Attendees retain full control through a per-device opt-out in the app.

entries.title: Ask scope for API tokens, For you feed controls, and push nudge settings
entries.summary: Three additions for the Ask (organizer Q&A) feature. **Org Settings → API Tokens**: a new **Opt-in** section lets admins tick **Ask (organizer Q&A)** (`read:ask`) on individual tokens; it is off by default and not included in the standard read-only or all-scopes sets. **Attend app settings → For you**: controls for max cards, card-type order (drag or up/down buttons), and an **Allow one sponsored card** toggle. **Attend app settings → Push nudges**: per-kind switches for free-slot suggestions, starts-soon reminders, and nearby prompts, plus optional quiet hours. Attendee activity history gains **"Changed suggestion and reminder notifications"** and **"Asked for fewer suggestions like this"** entries, and the sponsor placements list gains a **For you feed** slot.

where.path: Attend → App Settings (For you / Push nudges); Org Settings → API Tokens (read:ask scope)

entries.use_case: Organizers running the Attend app can now fine-tune what the For you feed shows each attendee and control whether push nudges fire — and which kinds — without contacting support. Teams building integrations against the Ask Q&A feature can scope API tokens to only that surface, keeping token permissions narrow.

cs_action.note: The read:ask scope requires web-api #4635 to be live before tokens using it will work; creating a token with it ticked will 400 until that API release ships. For you and nudges cards hide automatically when the API does not return the expected settings keys, so older API versions degrade gracefully.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using the Attend app asks how to control the For you feed or push notifications, or when a developer asks about scoping API access to Ask.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Attend beta who want granular control over attendee recommendations and notifications, and developers building integrations against the Ask Q&A endpoint.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → App Settings → For you / Push nudges; Org → Settings → API Tokens → Opt-in section
internal.gotchas: read:ask is intentionally excluded from ALL_SCOPE_VALUES and READ_SCOPE_VALUES — a new token does not get it unless the admin explicitly ticks it. Legacy tokens with no scopes stay [] and will receive 403 SCOPE_REQUIRED from the public API. The For you feed sponsor placement slot only appears when the placements API lists it in slots; older API versions never show it.
internal.talk_track: You can now set exactly how many and which types of cards appear in each attendee's For you feed, turn push nudges on or off per kind, and set quiet hours — all from the app settings panel. If you're building an integration that reads Ask answers, you can now create a token scoped only to that, so it can't touch anything else in your event.

draft.docs_gap: The Ask guide should add sections covering: (1) the read:ask API token scope and its opt-in behaviour; (2) For you feed settings (max cards, card-type order, sponsored card toggle); (3) Push nudges settings (per-kind switches, quiet hours); and (4) the For you feed sponsor placement slot.
draft.why_use_it: Ask is the AI-powered Q&A assistant inside the Attend app that answers attendee questions using your event content. The For you feed and push nudges settings let you decide how proactively the app surfaces sessions and reminders, so attendees get relevant suggestions without feeling overwhelmed. Scoping API tokens to `read:ask` means third-party tools can query Ask answers without gaining access to the rest of your event data.

entries.title: Control what Agenda, People and Partners pages list — and add custom list pages — in the mobile app builder
entries.summary: Organizers can now set **What this page shows** on the built-in **Agenda**, **People** and **Partners** pages: pick filter chips from the event's own data, choose **Sort by** (with direction), **Group by**, and **Reset** to defaults. A **Shows N of M** count reflects the same data the live app draws. Use **+ Add page** to create additional list pages (Sessions, People, Exhibitors, Sponsors, Products or Posters), give each a name, icon, template and its own filters, and reorder them under the built-ins. Every destination picker — tiles, band targets and **Tabs** — offers custom pages as **Page: \<title\>**. Turning a page off or deleting it shows a confirmation dialog listing every home button, band and tab that links to it, and removes those links automatically on save.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable list pages; then Event → Attend → App → Design

entries.use_case: Events with multiple session tracks, exhibitor tiers or sponsor categories can surface curated sub-lists — for example a "Poster Sessions" page filtered to that format, or a "Gold Sponsors" page — without requiring attendees to search or scroll through everything. Organizers control exactly what each list page shows and how it is sorted and grouped, matching the app's content to the event's programme structure.

cs_action.note: The list pages feature is gated behind layout_options.list_kinds from the API. Confirm the API PR (sessionboard-web-api#4637) is deployed and the flag is enabled for the customer's org before walking them through the builder.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to show different session types or sponsor tiers as separate pages in the app, or when they want to hide certain content from a list without removing it from search.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Attend Mobile App (beta) who have complex programmes — multiple tracks, poster sessions, tiered sponsors or exhibitors — and want attendees to navigate directly to curated lists.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → App → Design → Pages → [page] → What this page shows
internal.gotchas: The 'Shows N of M' count is hidden when a filter uses Who's Who groups or halls (map levels), because those IDs are not in the app bundle. Custom pages require the mobile app branch feature/app-list-pages; the mobile PR was not yet open at merge time — confirm mobile support is live before enabling for customers. Deleting or disabling a page automatically removes all links to it in the same draft save; warn customers to review their navigation layout after any page deletion.
internal.talk_track: You can now build a 'Keynotes only' agenda page, a 'Gold Sponsors' page and a 'Poster Gallery' page — each with its own filters and sort — and link to them from your home screen tiles or tab bar. The builder shows you exactly how many sessions or people each filter returns before you publish.

draft.docs_gap: The Design the event app guide should add a section covering the "What this page shows" panel (filters, sort, group, reset, Shows N of M), the "+ Add page" flow (type picker, naming, reordering), per-page inspector options (name, icon, Show in the app, Template, Delete), the confirmation dialog for disabling or deleting a page, and how custom pages appear in destination pickers.
draft.why_use_it: The mobile app builder lets you shape every list page attendees see — filtering by track, format, day, sponsor tier and more — so the app reflects your event's structure rather than showing a single undifferentiated list. Custom pages let you add as many focused views as your programme needs, each with its own name, icon and template. Because the filter preview counts records from the same data bundle the live app uses, what you see in the builder is exactly what attendees see on their phones.

entries.title: New "For you" home block surfaces personalised session and exhibitor cards in the attendee app
entries.summary: A new **For you** block is added to the attendee app's home screen, showing up to six personalised cards chosen from four types: **Next up**, **Gap filler**, **Topic match**, and **Exhibitor match**. Organizers control the block through **Attend → App Settings → For You** (`enabled`, `max_cards` 1–12, card type order). A sponsored **Exhibitor match** card can appear when a sponsor's topic or saved-session overlap matches the attendee; it is capped at one per feed and never shown as the only card. Attendees can dismiss cards with **Fewer like this**, which suppresses that target or card type from future feeds. Organizers can sell the `for_you` placement slot through **Attend → Sponsor Ads**.

where.path: Attend → App → Home (For you block) · Attend → App Settings → For You

entries.use_case: Events with large session catalogs can surface the right content to each attendee without requiring them to search. Organizers can also monetize the block by placing a single relevant sponsor card alongside organic recommendations.

cs_action.note: The block is on by default for all Attend (beta) events. The mobile client (WP27) and the settings UI (web-ui-v2) are follow-up work items — the API is live but the app render and the organizer settings screen are not yet shipped. Confirm both are live before promoting to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to help attendees discover sessions in a large catalog, or when a sponsor asks about in-app placement options beyond banner ads.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Attend (beta) events with 30+ sessions or exhibitors, and customers selling sponsor placements in the app.
internal.staff_path: Event → Attend → App Settings → For You; Event → Attend → Sponsor Ads → for_you slot
internal.gotchas: The mobile app render (WP27) and the organizer For You / nudges settings UI are not yet shipped — the API is ready but customers cannot see the block or configure it from the UI until those follow-up PRs land. Nudges settings are stored but not yet consumed (WP26). The 'for_you' slot does not appear in the placements slot picker until the web-ui-v2 follow-up ships.
internal.talk_track: The app now has a For you section on the home screen that picks the best sessions and exhibitors for each attendee based on their topics and schedule — and if you have a sponsor whose profile matches an attendee's interests, they can appear there too, with a single clearly-labelled card.

draft.docs_gap: The Recommend sessions and exhibitors guide should add a section covering the For you home block: how the four card types work, how organizers configure max_cards and card order, how the sponsored exhibitor match card is gated on relevance, and how attendee feedback (Fewer like this) suppresses future cards.
draft.why_use_it: The For you block removes the burden of discovery from attendees by surfacing a short, personalised feed of sessions and exhibitors matched to their interests, saved items, and schedule gaps. It uses the same topic-matching and organizer pin/boost/hide rules as the main recommendations engine, so the content always reflects your curation decisions. Sponsors can appear in the feed only when they are genuinely relevant to the attendee, keeping the experience useful rather than interruptive. Attendees who dismiss a card teach the feed to improve, reducing repeat suggestions they do not want.

entries.title: Filter, sort, group and create custom list pages in the Attend app
entries.summary: Organizers can now configure **filter**, **sort** and **group by** options on the built-in **Agenda**, **People** and **Partners** pages in the Attend app editor, and create up to 20 **custom list pages** (sessions, posters, people, exhibitors, sponsors or products) with their own title, icon, template, filters, sort order and grouping. Custom pages can be linked from tiles, navigation bands and tabs; the app validates that any linked page exists and is enabled before publishing.
entries.use_case: Events that want to surface a curated subset of sessions — such as only workshop-format sessions or sessions on a specific track — can create a dedicated custom page with pre-applied filters so attendees land directly on the right content without searching. Organizers running multi-format events can also give exhibitors and sponsors separate, independently sorted list pages.

cs_action.note: This is the API half only; the companion UI PR (web-ui-v2 feature/app-list-pages-builder) and mobile PR are still in progress. Do not demo or promise GA until all three are merged.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to show a filtered or curated subset of sessions, people or exhibitors in their Attend app, or wants separate navigation pages for different content types.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend mobile app (beta) who want more control over app navigation and content curation.
internal.gotchas: Custom pages carry filter values (track IDs, room IDs, tier IDs, etc.) verbatim when an event is cloned — filtered pages will show no results for remapped fields until an organizer edits the filter on the clone. Push-notification targets still only accept the three built-in page destinations; custom page IDs cannot be used as push-notification targets yet.
internal.talk_track: You can now build a custom 'Workshops' page that only shows workshop-format sessions, or a 'Diamond Sponsors' page filtered to your top tier — and link those pages directly from your app's home screen tiles or bottom navigation.

draft.docs_gap: The Design the event app guide should add a section covering how to configure filter, sort and group options on built-in pages, and how to create, configure and link custom list pages (including supported templates, filter fields per content kind, sort keys, group keys, and the enabled/disabled toggle).
draft.why_use_it: The Attend app's list pages let you control exactly what attendees see and how they navigate your content. Filter built-in pages to show only the sessions, people or partners that matter to a given audience, or build custom pages that group content by day, track, tier or category. Because each page can be linked from tiles, bands and tabs, you can design an app experience that guides attendees through your program without them needing to search.

entries.title: Embed the Ask AI assistant on your own website
entries.summary: A new anonymous **Ask** widget can be embedded on an Attend customer's own website, letting visitors ask questions about the event program without signing in. Organizers create and manage **embed keys** (with per-origin CORS restrictions and per-IP rate limits) to control where the widget may appear; the widget surfaces public program content, public knowledge-base answers, and pinned answers tagged **public**.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the Ask embed widget; then Event → Settings → Ask → Embed Keys

entries.use_case: Event teams that publish a public-facing event website can embed the Ask widget so prospective and registered attendees can get instant answers about the schedule, speakers, and logistics without leaving the site or signing in to the app.

cs_action.note: Admin UI for creating embed keys and marking info-page blocks as public is not yet shipped (ADM side pending). The API and embed runtime are live but the full self-serve flow requires the forthcoming admin UI PR.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to add an AI chat widget to their event website or wants to surface Ask outside the Attend app.
internal.who_should_get_it: Attend customers who have a public event website and want to let anonymous visitors query the program via AI.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Ask → Embed Keys (once admin UI ships)
internal.gotchas: The admin UI to create embed keys and to mark info-page layout blocks as public is not in this PR — customers cannot self-serve yet. Voice is always returned in config (no voice-off switch on the public profile yet). EU and Middle East deployments get local-only voice (device STT, browser TTS). Non-public info pages are never exposed even if queried by name.
internal.talk_track: You can embed an Ask chat widget on your own event website so visitors get instant AI answers about your program. You control which domains can host it, set spending limits per key, and only content you mark as public is ever shared.

draft.docs_gap: The Ask guide should add a section covering the website embed widget: how to create and rotate embed keys, how to mark info-page blocks as public, CORS origin restrictions, per-IP rate limits, and the difference between the in-app Ask experience and the anonymous website widget.
draft.why_use_it: Ask lets visitors to your event website get instant, AI-powered answers about the program — sessions, speakers, and event logistics — without signing in. You control exactly which websites may host the widget by listing allowed origins on each embed key, and only content you have explicitly marked public is ever surfaced. Per-IP rate limits and per-key budgets keep usage predictable and prevent abuse.

entries.title: Query event data with Ask via the public API
entries.summary: A new `POST /v1/event/:eventId/ask` endpoint lets API integrations send natural-language questions about an event and receive AI-generated answers. The token must include the **`read:ask`** scope; legacy no-scope tokens receive a `403 SCOPE_REQUIRED` response. A rate limit of 100 requests per 15 minutes applies, and the org-level AI kill switch is respected.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the read:ask scope on your API token; then use POST /v1/event/:eventId/ask

entries.use_case: Teams building custom integrations or internal tools can now send natural-language questions about an event directly through the API and surface AI-generated answers in their own applications, without requiring a user to be logged into Sessionboard.

cs_action.note: The dependent web-api PR #4635 was not merged at the time this PR shipped; the route returns 404 until that PR is live. Confirm both are deployed before promoting to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks about querying event data programmatically with natural language, or when they are building a custom integration that needs AI-powered Q&A on top of their event content.
internal.who_should_get_it: Technically sophisticated customers or partners who are already using the public API and want to expose Ask functionality in their own tools.
internal.gotchas: Requires the read:ask scope to be explicitly added to the token — legacy no-scope tokens get 403. The org AI kill switch blocks the route with 403 AI_DISABLED. Rate limit is 100 requests per 15 minutes. The question text is redacted from audit logs. The 90-second upstream timeout is specific to this route. web-api #4635 must also be merged and deployed for the route to return anything other than 404.
internal.talk_track: You can now call a single API endpoint with a plain-English question about your event and get an AI-generated answer back — useful for building internal chatbots, dashboards, or automated reports without logging into Sessionboard.

draft.docs_gap: The API tokens guide should document the new read:ask scope, the POST /v1/event/:eventId/ask endpoint (request shape, response shape, error codes including 422, 429 RATE_LIMITED, 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED, 403 AI_DISABLED), the 100-per-15-min rate limit, and the 90-second timeout behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: The Sessionboard public API lets you read and write event data programmatically, so your own tools and workflows stay in sync with what is happening in Sessionboard. With the Ask endpoint, you can go further and ask plain-language questions about your event data from any application that can make an HTTP request. Use it to power internal dashboards, chatbots, or automated reporting pipelines that need answers drawn from your event content.

entries.title: Schedule Itinerary embed now always shows sessions in chronological order within each hour
entries.summary: In the **Schedule Itinerary** embed, sessions within an hour row (e.g. "11:00 AM") were being reordered by the configured schedule sort — for example, a **Location** sort could push an 11:30 session above an 11:00 session. Sessions within each hour row now always appear in start-time order first; the configured schedule sort only breaks ties between sessions that share an identical start time.
entries.use_case: Events that sort their schedule embed by Track, Location, or another field were seeing sessions appear out of time order within an hour block on their website. This fix ensures attendees always see sessions listed earliest-to-latest within each hour, with the configured sort only applying when two sessions start at exactly the same time.

cs_action.note: Any event with a Schedule Itinerary embed that uses a non-Start-Time schedule sort (Track, Location, End Time, Session ID, etc.) will see the session order change within hour rows that mix start times. 14 embeds identified in one region (11 affected); second region count pending. Stale cached payloads rebuild on the next request — no manual cache purge needed for most customers, but support can purge embed-stale-v2:<id>:* for urgent cases.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their Schedule Itinerary embed is showing sessions out of time order, or asks why the order changed after this deploy.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using a Schedule Itinerary embed with a schedule-scope sort other than Start Time asc.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Embeds → [Schedule Itinerary embed] → Schedule sort setting
internal.gotchas: Cached embed payloads (stale copy up to 7 days, V1 URL cache up to 60 min) will serve the old order until the cache rebuilds naturally on the next request. For immediate QA or urgent customer requests, purge embed-stale-v2:<id>:* for the specific embed ID.
internal.talk_track: Sessions in your Schedule Itinerary embed now always appear in start-time order within each hour block. If you have a secondary sort configured (like Track or Location), it still applies — but only to break ties between sessions that start at exactly the same time.

draft.docs_gap: The Embeds guide should note that the Schedule Itinerary embed always orders sessions chronologically within each hour row, with the configured schedule sort acting only as a tiebreaker for sessions sharing an identical start time.
draft.why_use_it: null

entries.title: Import a pre-existing glossary into Taxonomy before running topic extraction
entries.summary: A new **Import glossary** button in **Settings → Library → Taxonomy** opens a dialog where organizers can paste terms (one per line, with an optional ` | description`) or upload a CSV (`term,description`) to seed the topic library before the AI extraction run. A preview shows the first 10 rows, flags duplicates and empty names, and disables submit when the batch exceeds 500 terms. After import, the result view lists created topics, skipped duplicates (with retired-topic flags), and invalid rows with readable reasons.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Generate Topics; then Settings → Library → Taxonomy → Import glossary

entries.use_case: Organizations that already maintain a controlled vocabulary or medical/industry glossary can load those terms directly into Taxonomy before the AI extraction run, ensuring the generated topic graph reflects their established terminology rather than starting from scratch.

cs_action.note: The companion API endpoint (sessionboard-web-api#4612) must be deployed before this UI is live; the Import glossary button returns a 404 until the API is released. Confirm API is live before pointing customers to this feature.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Generate Topics mentions they already have a controlled vocabulary, taxonomy, or glossary they want to preserve in the AI topic graph.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Generate Topics limited release who have an existing term list — medical societies, trade associations, or any org with a formal content taxonomy.
internal.gotchas: Submit is disabled for batches over 500 terms; customers with large glossaries will need to split imports. Retired topics that match an imported term are flagged as skipped in the result view — reassure customers the term already exists. No client-side file size cap yet (follow-up planned); advise customers to keep CSV files under ~1 MB.
internal.talk_track: If you already have a glossary or controlled vocabulary, you can paste it straight into Taxonomy before the AI runs — up to 500 terms at a time, with optional descriptions. The preview shows you exactly what will be created, skipped, or flagged as invalid before you commit.

draft.docs_gap: The closest article (/get-started/glossary) covers Sessionboard's own product glossary, not the Taxonomy feature. A dedicated guide for Settings → Library → Taxonomy should be created covering how to import a glossary, the paste and CSV formats, the 500-term cap, preview behaviour, and how imported topics interact with the AI extraction run.
draft.why_use_it: Taxonomy lets you build and manage a structured library of topics that the AI uses to tag sessions, speakers, and contacts. Seeding it with your own glossary before extraction means the AI works within your organization's established vocabulary from day one. You can paste terms by hand or upload a CSV, add optional descriptions, and review exactly what will be created before committing — keeping your topic library clean and authoritative.

entries.title: Import a pre-existing glossary into the Taxonomy topic library
entries.summary: A new **Import glossary** action in the Taxonomy library lets org admins upload up to 500 terms (name + optional description) via paste or CSV before running a topic-extraction job. The response shows which terms were **created**, which were **skipped** (already exist), and which rows were **invalid** (blank, too long, or duplicate within the file), so the valid ones are always saved even when some rows fail.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Generate Topics; then Settings → Library → Taxonomy → Import glossary

entries.use_case: Organizations that already maintain a controlled vocabulary or subject taxonomy can seed Sessionboard's topic library with their existing terms before the first AI extraction run, so the AI reuses and reinforces those terms rather than generating synonyms from scratch.

cs_action.note: A medium-severity security finding is open: the import endpoint currently requires only org membership, not the MANAGE_FIELDS permission that a topic-extraction run requires. Confirm the intended permission gate before promoting this to customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to pre-populate the topic library with their own taxonomy or controlled vocabulary before running Generate Topics for the first time.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on Generate Topics (limited release) who have an existing glossary, subject taxonomy, or controlled vocabulary they want the AI to respect.
internal.gotchas: 1) The companion UI PR must also be deployed — the button 404s until both API and UI are live. 2) If an imported term is later grouped with a shorter LLM-generated synonym, the display label may show the shorter name (accepted risk, no rename occurs). 3) Permission gate is currently org-membership only — follow up on whether MANAGE_FIELDS should be required.
internal.talk_track: If you already have a list of approved topics or a subject taxonomy, you can paste them straight into Sessionboard before your first extraction run. The library will mark each term as human-reviewed, protect it from pruning, and use it as a preference signal when the AI groups new submissions.

draft.docs_gap: The Glossary article does not cover the Taxonomy topic library or the Import glossary workflow; a new guide (or a dedicated section) should explain how to prepare a CSV, what the created/skipped/invalid response means, and how human-sourced terms interact with AI extraction runs.
draft.why_use_it: The Taxonomy library is where Sessionboard stores the topics used to tag sessions, surface recommendations, and power AI-driven content grouping. Seeding it with your organization's own controlled vocabulary before extraction runs means the AI works within your preferred terminology from day one. You can import up to 500 terms at once — with optional descriptions — and the library flags duplicates and invalid rows without discarding the valid ones. Human-sourced terms are protected from automatic pruning, so your glossary stays intact across extraction cycles.

entries.title: CMS Search Graph adds sponsor/exhibitor layers, speaker role labels on edges, a View all button, and a hidden-connections note
entries.summary: The **CMS Search › Graph** view gains five improvements: (1) **Sponsor** and **Exhibitor** layer chips (off by default) plot sponsor and exhibitor nodes with their tier shown beneath the name; (2) edges between speakers and sessions are coloured and labelled by role (**Speaker**, **Moderator**, **Chairperson**, or custom role), with one curved edge per role when a speaker holds several roles in one session; (3) a **View all** button in the top-left of the canvas returns to the full overview after isolating a node or re-centring, keeping current layers, depth and filters; (4) a **"+N more connections not shown at this depth"** note appears in the side detail panel for nodes at the depth boundary so the cut-off is explained without covering the canvas; (5) the graph now centres instantly on first render instead of appearing in the corner and zooming out after a delay.
entries.use_case: Organizers exploring the knowledge graph can now see how sponsors and exhibitors connect to sessions and speakers, understand exactly what role each speaker plays in a session at a glance, and navigate back to the full graph after drilling into a single node — all without losing their current filter and depth settings.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to visualise sponsor or exhibitor relationships in their program, or when they want to see speaker roles on the graph rather than just speaker names.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who actively use the CMS Search Graph to explore program relationships, especially those with sponsors, exhibitors, or sessions with multiple participant roles.
internal.gotchas: Sponsor and Exhibitor layers are off by default — customers must toggle them on in the layer chips. Custom roles inherit their core role's colour (speaker/moderator/chairperson). The '+N more connections' note only appears when the API returns the hidden_connections field; older API versions will simply not show it.
internal.talk_track: The graph now shows your sponsors and exhibitors as nodes you can explore, labels each speaker edge with their exact role, and gives you a one-click way back to the full picture after you've drilled into a single node.

draft.docs_gap: The Program Site guide does not document the CMS Search Graph view at all; a dedicated section or guide should cover the layer toggles (including Sponsor and Exhibitor), edge role colouring, the View all button, the depth boundary note, and how to navigate the graph.
draft.why_use_it: The CMS Search Graph gives you a visual map of how sessions, speakers, sponsors, exhibitors and other entities in your event relate to one another. Use it to spot gaps in your program, verify that the right speakers are linked to the right sessions with the right roles, and explore how sponsors and exhibitors connect to your content. The depth controls and layer toggles let you focus on exactly the slice of the program you care about.

entries.title: Sponsors and exhibitors appear in the CMS Search graph, with a fix for nodes showing "Unnamed" labels
entries.summary: The **Graph** explorer in CMS Search now includes **Sponsor** and **Exhibitor** as focusable, searchable node types. Each sponsor node shows the sessions it sponsors; each exhibitor node shows the event it exhibits at and, when the Session layer is on, the individual sessions. A new **+N more connections** indicator appears on frontier nodes to show how many additional neighbours exist beyond the current depth. A bug that caused topic and event nodes to render as "Unnamed topic" / "Unnamed event" when the Session layer was enabled has been fixed.
entries.use_case: Organizers using the graph explorer to understand content relationships can now see how sponsors and exhibitors connect to sessions and events, and can spot when a speaker or sponsor has more connections than the current depth reveals.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why sponsors or exhibitors are missing from the graph, or reports that topic/event nodes show as 'Unnamed' with the Session layer on.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the CMS Search graph who also have Sponsors or Exhibitors enabled.
internal.staff_path: CMS → Search → Graph → enable Sponsor or Exhibitor layer
internal.gotchas: Sponsor and Exhibitor node types are not in the default layers — users must explicitly enable the layer. The '+N more connections' count is only shown on last-hop nodes and is suppressed when the graph was truncated by the node limit.
internal.talk_track: You can now pull sponsors and exhibitors into the graph to see exactly which sessions they're tied to, and the graph will tell you when there are more connections just outside the current depth so you know when to drill deeper.

draft.docs_gap: The Program Site guide (or a dedicated Graph explorer guide) should document the Sponsor and Exhibitor layer options, the "+N more connections" indicator, and note that these layers are not on by default.
draft.why_use_it: The graph explorer in CMS Search lets you visualise the relationships between sessions, speakers, topics, sponsors, and exhibitors across your event. Use it to discover which sponsors are tied to the most sessions, which speakers share topic clusters, or how exhibitors are distributed across the program. Focusing on any node expands its neighbourhood so you can trace connections without leaving the page.

entries.title: Reviewers are notified when a participant uploads a file or a build is returned
entries.summary: Two new automatic notifications are sent to reviewers on Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans. **Evaluator: Session File Uploaded** alerts reviewers on an open round (with uploaded files enabled) whenever a participant uploads a file — the uploader is not notified. **Evaluator: Build Returned** alerts the team lead when a session build is returned, including the reason. Both notifications appear in each reviewer's **Notification Preferences** profile toggle and can be managed there.
entries.use_case: Reviewers on active rounds no longer need to check back manually to see if a speaker has uploaded new materials or if a build they submitted was sent back. The notifications keep reviewers in the loop in real time so nothing falls through the cracks before a round closes.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans asks how reviewers are kept informed about new uploads or returned builds.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans where participants upload files for review or where team leads manage session builds.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Rounds; reviewer notification preferences in their portal profile
internal.gotchas: The file-upload notification only fires for open v2 rounds that have 'uploaded files' enabled. The uploader (participant/speaker) is deliberately not notified — only reviewers on that round receive it.
internal.talk_track: Reviewers on your active evaluation rounds will now get an automatic alert whenever a speaker uploads a file, so they can score it right away. And if a team lead returns a build, the lead gets notified with the reason — no more chasing people down.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the two new evaluator notification types — session file uploaded and build returned — including which role receives each, the conditions that trigger them, and how reviewers can manage their preferences.
draft.why_use_it: Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans let you run structured, multi-round reviews with scorecards and team leads. These notifications ensure reviewers are alerted the moment new content is available to score or a build requires their attention, reducing the back-and-forth between organizers and review teams during an active evaluation cycle.

entries.title: Add web pages, PDFs, Word files and FAQ lists as knowledge sources for the Ask AI assistant
entries.summary: Organizers can now upload PDF or DOCX files, paste a web page URL, or build an FAQ list as **Knowledge Sources** for the Ask AI assistant. The assistant searches these documents when answering attendee questions and cites the passage it used. Sources go through a **draft → pending → ready** lifecycle so nothing reaches attendees until an organizer explicitly approves and tags it for the **attendee** audience. A nightly refresh keeps URL-based sources current.
entries.use_case: Events with exhibitor manuals, speaker guides, venue FAQs or policy documents can surface that content directly inside the attendee Ask assistant, so attendees get accurate, cited answers without staff having to monitor every question.

cs_action.note: Knowledge sources are available to any event using Attend + Ask, but organizers must explicitly approve (set status to 'pending' → 'ready') and tag each source for the attendee audience before it surfaces. Nothing is shown to attendees automatically.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how attendees can get answers about venue logistics, exhibitor policies, or event FAQs without emailing the team.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers already using the Attend app with Ask enabled who have reference documents (PDFs, Word files, web pages, or FAQ lists) they want attendees to be able to query.
internal.gotchas: Files must be PDF or DOCX and ≤ 25 MB. A source stays invisible to attendees until its status is 'ready' and it is tagged for the 'attendee' audience. If a source is removed or re-ingested after an attendee conversation, the cited passage disappears from that conversation's history too — old chunk IDs are invalidated on re-ingest.
internal.talk_track: You can upload your exhibitor manual or paste your venue FAQ page, approve it, and from that point on Ask will find the right passage and show attendees exactly where the answer came from — no more 'email us for details'.

draft.docs_gap: The Ask guide should add a section explaining how to create, approve and manage Knowledge Sources (web pages, PDFs, DOCX files, FAQ lists), the draft → pending → ready lifecycle, audience tagging, the 25 MB file limit, and how cited passages appear in attendee answers.
draft.why_use_it: Ask lets attendees get instant answers to event questions from inside the mobile app. Adding knowledge sources means the assistant draws on your own documents — exhibitor manuals, venue guides, FAQ lists, speaker policies — rather than only the structured program data. You control exactly what attendees can see by tagging and approving each source before it goes live, and the assistant always shows the passage it cited so attendees can read the original.

entries.title: AI assistant (Ask) is now available in the Sites participant portal
entries.summary: Participants signed in to a Sites portal can now use the **Ask** AI assistant to get answers about their tasks, CFP submissions, sessions, and pinned knowledge — without leaving the portal. The assistant supports text, voice, and live-agent handoff, and is scoped to each participant's own data only. Organizers must save and enable a portal AI profile before the assistant becomes active.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the Sites portal assistant; then Sites → [site] → Assistant → Profile → save and enable

entries.use_case: Participants attending a multi-event site can ask the assistant about their open tasks, submission status, and session details in plain language instead of hunting through the portal. Organizers can offer a branded, AI-powered concierge experience without any additional support overhead.

cs_action.note: The virtual AI profile is off by default. An organizer must explicitly save and enable a profile for the site before any AI spend occurs. Confirm the customer has reviewed and enabled the profile before going live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer running a Sites portal asks how to reduce participant support volume or wants to offer a self-serve help experience inside the portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Sites (program sites / CFP portals) who have participants with tasks, submissions, or session assignments and want to offer AI-assisted self-service.
internal.gotchas: The assistant is off by default even after the feature is enabled — the organizer must save and enable a profile. The assistant returns 404 to the portal launcher if no role on the site has an assistant configured, so the chat button stays hidden until setup is complete. draft.why_use_it: The Ask assistant in the Sites portal gives participants a conversational way to navigate their tasks, submissions, and sessions. It answers questions using only the participant's own data — tasks, CFP applications, session assignments, and pinned knowledge — so answers are always relevant and private. When a question needs a human, participants can hand off directly to the event coordinator inbox from the same chat window. Voice input is also supported for hands-free use.

entries.title: Compare your event's topics against a competitor event's sessions
entries.summary: Organizers using Speaker Prospects can now open a competitor (external) event and see a **Topic Comparison** — which topics only the competitor covers, which only your event covers, and affinity matches that pair similar-but-differently-named topic clusters across both programmes. A separate **Topic Convergence** view groups both events' topics into thematic families, writes a one-sentence focus characterisation for each event, and proposes up to three concrete moves to close the content gap. Topics are also extracted automatically from competitor sessions via the existing `generate_topics` pipeline, and the **Topics** list now shows an **External Session Count** column alongside the existing usage count.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Generate Topics; then Prospects → External Events → [event] → Topic Comparison / Topic Convergence

where.path: Prospects → External Events → [competitor event] → Topic Comparison / Topic Convergence

entries.use_case: Programme teams researching competitor events can instantly see which topic areas a rival conference emphasises that their own event does not, and get AI-generated suggestions for where to shift or expand their content strategy to close the gap.

cs_action.note: Requires the org-level `feature--generate_topics` flag. Keep `TAXONOMY_EXTERNAL_SESSIONS_MAX_PER_RUN=0` in Doppler until every worker image is on this release, then set it to the desired cap. Do NOT enable for orgs that only have the contact-topics flag without explicit product sign-off — the unified flag would send contact bios to the LLM.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how their programme compares to a specific competitor event, or when they are building their CFP and want to identify content gaps.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Speaker Prospects and Generate Topics already enabled who actively track competitor events.

External session topic counts are shown in a separate `External Session Count` column and intentionally excluded from the existing `usage_count` to avoid inflating internal topic usage stats. Two product conflicts are pending sign-off: the unified feature flag and whether competitor text should mint new org topics.
internal.talk_track: You can now pull up any competitor event in Prospects and see a side-by-side topic breakdown — what they cover that you don't, what you cover that they don't, and where your topic clusters are close enough to compete. The Convergence view then groups everything into themes and tells you exactly where the biggest content gaps are and what moves would close them.

draft.docs_gap: The Speaker Prospects section of the help centre has no guide covering External Events, topic comparison, or topic convergence — a new article should document how to open a competitor event's Topic Comparison and Topic Convergence views, what the affinity matches and convergence moves mean, and how topics are extracted from competitor sessions.
draft.why_use_it: Speaker Prospects lets you track competitor events and the speakers who appear at them. The topic comparison and convergence tools extend that intelligence to the content layer: you can see at a glance where a rival event's programme diverges from yours, identify adjacent topic clusters that could attract the same audience, and get structured recommendations for closing the gap — all without leaving Sessionboard.

entries.title: Field Rules editor now loads archived fields and recovers from API errors

Messaging lets participants and organizers continue conversations in context — participants see their own thread history and can reply, while organizers receive notifications through their existing inbox. Org-level and Site-level assistant profiles let you define the assistant's tone and knowledge once and have it apply across every program on the Site.

entries.title: Participants can read and reply to organizer messages in the portal
entries.summary: A **Messages** section is now available in the signed-in Sites portal. Participants and awards entrants who sent a question through the **Ask** panel can open the conversation, read the organizer's reply, and send a follow-up — all without leaving the portal. The sidebar shows a **Messages** entry with an unread-count badge, and the **Ask** panel's confirmation screen links directly to the new thread.
