draft.why_use_it: The Messages inbox gives portal participants a single place to track every conversation they have started with the organizer — whether through a general Ask question or an awards-related enquiry. Threads are grouped by topic, unread replies are highlighted with a badge, and participants can reply directly from the thread view. This keeps communication in context alongside tasks, forms, and other portal content.

entries.title: Embed the Ask AI assistant on any website with a one-line script
entries.summary: A new embeddable widget lets organizers place the event's **Ask** AI assistant on any external website by adding a single `<script>` tag. The floating launcher opens a chat panel with streaming answers, **citation cards** (session, speaker, exhibitor, sponsor, document, organizer-pinned, and transcript sources), **suggested questions**, and action links such as **Add to my schedule**. The launcher is automatically hidden when the embed key is invalid or the assistant is unavailable. Voice input uses on-device speech recognition only; Arabic layouts render right-to-left automatically.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the Ask embed; then copy the script snippet from your embed settings and paste it into your website's HTML

entries.use_case: Organizers who publish a conference website outside Sessionboard can surface the Ask assistant there without rebuilding their site. Attendees get instant, cited answers about sessions, speakers, and exhibitors directly on the event website.

cs_action.note: The embed API key (ask_pk_…) must be provisioned and the origin domain allow-listed before the launcher will appear. A 403 from the config endpoint silently hides the launcher, so customers will see nothing without this step.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to put the Ask assistant on their own conference website or a third-party event site.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who have Ask enabled in the Attend app and also maintain an external event website where they want to surface AI-powered Q&A for attendees.
internal.gotchas: Voice input is local-only (Web Speech API, on-device recognition); relay-based STT is not yet wired up. The mic is hidden entirely if the browser does not support on-device recognition or if the config sets voice: false. Socket.IO relay is marked TODO in the codebase — do not promise cloud-based voice transcription.
internal.talk_track: Drop one script tag on your event website and your attendees get a floating Ask button. They can type a question and get a streamed answer with clickable citation cards — session titles, speaker bios, exhibitor pages — plus a direct link to add a session to their schedule. The launcher disappears on its own if the key isn't valid, so there's no broken widget to worry about.

draft.docs_gap: The Embeds guide should add a dedicated section for the Ask embed covering: the script-tag snippet and its attributes (data-key, data-lang, data-api-url), how to obtain an embed key, the origin allow-list requirement, citation card types, voice limitations (on-device only), RTL language support, and the "launcher does not appear" troubleshooting steps already documented in EMBED_INTEGRATION.md.
draft.why_use_it: The Ask embed brings the event's AI assistant to any website with a single script tag, so attendees can get instant answers about sessions, speakers, and exhibitors without leaving the page they are already on. Answers stream in real time and include citation cards that link back to the original source — a session detail, a speaker profile, an exhibitor listing, or an organizer-pinned note — so attendees always know where the information came from. Suggested questions help first-time visitors know what to ask, and action links let them add sessions to their schedule in one tap. The launcher respects the event's language settings and hides itself automatically when the assistant is not configured or available, so there is nothing to clean up if the feature is turned off.

entries.title: Blind-review anonymity, reminder accuracy, and reviewer notifications corrected for evaluation plans
entries.summary: Seven bugs in Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans are fixed: reviewers with a blind-review assignment on a session now receive a **"A participant"** attribution (with no sender identity) when a file is uploaded, instead of seeing the uploader's name. **Session File Uploaded** notifications are no longer sent to reviewers in rounds whose window has already closed. Org-level reminder emails (**Monday summary** and **due-soon reminder**) now count only live, unmerged submissions and link to the correct portal site rather than an org gallery. A reviewer enrolled in both a v1 and a v2 plan can no longer be double-counted toward the minimum-reviews threshold, preventing premature score exposure. The **Preview** score count now reflects only completed reviews from the last scored round, matching the feedback payload.

where.path: Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Rounds / Evaluators / Preview

entries.use_case: Events running blind reviews need confidence that reviewer anonymity is never accidentally broken by a file-upload notification. Organizers relying on weekly reminder emails need accurate submission counts and working portal links so reviewers can act on them without confusion.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that blind-review anonymity was broken via file-upload emails, that reminder emails showed wrong submission counts or broken portal links, or that scores became visible too early.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Sessions 2.0 evaluation plans, especially those with blind-review rounds, multi-plan reviewers, or org-level reminder emails enabled.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Rounds / Evaluators / Preview
internal.gotchas: The double-counting fix applies to reviewers who appear in both a v1 and a v2 plan on the same event — they now count once toward review_min_reviews, so a minimum of 2 genuinely requires 2 distinct people. Orgs that had inflated reminder counts will now see lower (correct) numbers.
internal.talk_track: If you run blind reviews, file-upload notifications no longer reveal who uploaded — reviewers see 'A participant' instead of a name. Reminder emails now count only active submissions and link directly to the right reviewer portal.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add a note that blind-round reviewers receive anonymised file-upload notices ("A participant") and that Session File Uploaded notifications are suppressed for rounds outside their active window.
draft.why_use_it: Round-based evaluation plans let you run structured, multi-stage review cycles with configurable scorecards, blind-review modes, and automated reminders — all without exposing scores or identities before the right moment. Use them when you need fine-grained control over who sees what, when scores become visible, and how reviewers are reminded to complete their work.

entries.title: 13 platform UI fixes: search markup, bell popover, event creation recovery, colour field validation, and more
entries.summary: A batch of 13 targeted fixes across the platform. Highlights: **Global Search** (Cmd+K) no longer renders raw `<b>`/`<i>` tags in result titles — only the yellow highlight mark is kept. The **notification bell** popover stays on-screen at narrow (390 px) viewports. **Add Event** now retries silently on server errors and, if the event cannot be confirmed, tells you to check **Events** rather than showing a generic failure. The **Site colour field** shows an inline error for invalid hex values and refuses to save them. **Community** date headings now respect the UI language (French and Spanish were showing English dates). The **Open a form** picker matches on form ID and labels duplicate-named forms with **ID NNNN**. The **Credits** panel in the session drawer is now gated on the org-level Credits flag. The **Domains** settings page shows the email domain panel whenever the event switch, the org feature, or an existing custom sender is present. Saving intake sections skips the email notification and says so when no one could be emailed. The coordinator stale-draft error is now translated (de/fr/es). The Roles settings sheet stays open and surfaces the error when saving fails. The no-access page for an unknown event suppresses raw 404 toasts.
entries.use_case: These fixes remove a set of confusing or broken behaviours that organizers and participants encounter during everyday use — from garbled search results and off-screen popovers to silent save failures and raw error JSON on the no-access page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Raise individual items if a customer reports one of the specific broken behaviours listed in the summary.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — fixes are default-on across org and event contexts.

SB-9948 (Add Event recovery) only triggers on 5xx / 409 / no-response — normal creates are unchanged. SB-9882 (Domains panel) removes the super-user bypass, so the panel now shows for regular admins who meet any of the three conditions.
internal.talk_track: We shipped a wave of platform polish fixes — the most visible ones are: search results no longer show raw HTML tags, the notification bell stays on-screen on small displays, and the Add Event flow recovers gracefully from server hiccups instead of showing a failure toast.

The /settings/domains guide should note that the email domain panel appears whenever the event switch, the org feature, or an existing custom sender is active — not only for super-users. entries.title: Brella connector: duplicate-mapping guard, time-zone warnings, credential verification, and custom-field warnings
entries.summary: Four fixes to the Brella integration: (1) **Map events** now blocks mapping the same Sessionboard event or the same Brella event more than once across all connections in the org, and returns a clear error naming the conflicting connection. (2) Mapping or editing a mapping where the Sessionboard and Brella event time zones differ now shows a warning toast naming both zones; every subsequent sync also writes a warning row in **Event → History → Integrations**. (3) Saving a Brella connection with an invalid token now returns a Brella-specific error message instead of a generic "domain and campaign" message, and the connection card shows a verified checkmark only after credentials pass; LiveBuzz connections show "saved · not verified yet" until the first mapping save confirms them. (4) When a sync sends a custom field key that Brella does not recognise, a record note and a warning row in **Sync History** name the unrecognised field instead of silently dropping the value. The **Check drift** button is hidden for Brella connections because Brella does not support drift detection.
entries.use_case: Organizers running multiple Brella connections for the same org can now trust that each Sessionboard event and each Brella event is mapped exactly once, that time-zone mismatches are surfaced before data drifts, and that custom-field sync failures are visible in Sync History rather than silently lost.

entries.title: Brella connector: four UI accuracy fixes for drift check, token verification, event mapping, and time-zone warnings
entries.summary: Four issues in the Brella integration UI are resolved. The **Check drift** button is now hidden for Brella connections (which do not support drift reads), so it no longer reports "checked 0". The API access token label now reads "**Brella API Access Token saved · not verified yet**" when the token was saved without being verified, instead of showing a false check mark. The **Map events** picker no longer lists events already mapped on another Brella connection. When a mapped event's time zone differs from the Brella event's time zone, a warning banner appears on the mapped-event row and at the top of **Event Settings**, and a toast is shown when the mapping is saved.

where.path: Apps → Brella → Connection card / Map events / Event Settings

entries.use_case: Organizers managing multiple Brella connections can now trust that the token verification status is accurate, that the event picker only shows unmapped events, and that any time-zone mismatch between Sessionboard and Brella is surfaced immediately — reducing silent sync errors before they reach attendees.

cs_action.note: Connections saved before the API deploy (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4629) will still show the old check-mark tick on the token label because the UI cannot determine whether they were verified. Advise customers to re-verify if they are unsure.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports confusing Brella sync results, a false token-verified tick, duplicate events appearing in the mapping picker, or no warning about time-zone mismatches.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Brella integration, especially those with multiple Brella connections mapping different events.
internal.gotchas: The token verification label fix requires the API PR (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#4629) to be deployed first for new connections; existing connections saved before that deploy will retain the old tick mark. The Check drift button is hidden for Brella regardless of API deploy order.
internal.talk_track: The Brella connector now shows accurate token verification status, hides events that are already mapped elsewhere, and warns you immediately if the time zones between your Sessionboard event and Brella event don't match — so you can catch configuration issues before running a sync.

draft.docs_gap: The Brella guide should document that Check drift is not available for Brella connections, explain the "saved · not verified yet" token label, note that already-mapped events are hidden from the Map events picker, and describe the time-zone warning banner and toast that appear when mapped events have mismatched time zones.

entries.title: Twelve fixes across Evaluations, Call for Reviewers, email campaigns, and event cloning
entries.summary: This release resolves twelve reported issues across several modules: **Call for Reviewers** now supports member-attribute gate rules (up to 10 conditions with inline validation) in call settings; email attachment lists show a **Move up / Move down** control per row and appear in the **Preview** and **Ready to send** steps; sent campaigns disable the attachments field so content cannot be edited after sending; the **Confirm** chip in **Send Email** counts only checked recipients; ballot-size validation shows an inline error immediately and scrolls to the field on a failed save; the org-level evaluation plan wizard shows the correct timezone under **Review period**; assignment filters no longer send incomplete rows that caused 400 errors; event-level evaluator identity dialogs use the correct event-scoped copy in all four languages; Round Settings strings are fully translated in German, Spanish, and French; merge tags over 200 characters are included in AI content checks; and the clone result panel now shows evaluator-copy warnings and conversion notes.

where.path: Sessions → Evaluation Plans | Call for Reviewers | Emails & Campaigns | Event Settings → Clone

entries.use_case: Organizers running evaluations, email campaigns, or cloning events will encounter fewer dead-ends: attachment ordering and previews work correctly in campaigns and one-off sends, ballot-size errors surface immediately, call-for-reviewer gate rules are now configurable in the UI, and clone reports surface evaluator-copy warnings so nothing is silently skipped.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports any of: attachments missing from email previews, attachment order not saving, sent campaign still showing an editable attachments field, ballot-size field not validating, CC count wrong in Send Email, 400 errors on assignment filters, wrong timezone in org plan wizard, German/Spanish/French strings showing English in Round Settings, clone not reporting evaluator warnings, or Call for Reviewers lacking attribute gate rules.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — these are bug fixes that are on by default.
internal.staff_path: Event → Sessions → Evaluation Plans → [plan] → Step 3 Rounds; Event → Call for Reviewers → Call Settings; Event → Emails & Campaigns; Org → Events → Clone
internal.gotchas: SB-9987 (ballot size 0 inline error) and SB-9988 (German Round Settings strings) still need a manual browser check per the PR notes — the jsdom symptom for 9987 did not fully reproduce. SB-9912 intake gate rules require the API-side PR (web-api#4628) to be deployed as well.
internal.talk_track: We shipped a batch of fixes this cycle covering evaluation plan setup, email attachment handling, and the clone report — if you have been hitting any of those rough edges they should be resolved now.

entries.title: Call for Reviewers closed early no longer shows a future close date
entries.summary: When an admin closes a Call for Reviewers before its scheduled close date, the public apply page now shows **"This call is no longer accepting applications."** instead of "This call closed on [future date]." The dated message only appears once the close date has actually passed. Custom closed copy is unaffected.

where.path: Evaluations → Call for Reviewers → [call] → public apply link

entries.use_case: If an event team closes a reviewer call early — for example, because enough reviewers have signed up — applicants visiting the public link will now see a clear, accurate message rather than a confusing future date.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their reviewer apply page showed a future date after they manually closed the call early.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Call for Reviewers who closes a call before its scheduled close date.
internal.staff_path: Event → Evaluations → Call for Reviewers → [call] → close the call in admin → visit the public apply link
internal.gotchas: Custom closed copy set by the organizer is not affected by this fix — it always displays as entered.
internal.talk_track: If you close a reviewer call early, applicants will now see a neutral 'no longer accepting applications' message instead of a confusing future date.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the closed message shown to applicants depends on whether the close date has passed: a future close date shows a generic "no longer accepting" message, while a past close date shows the specific date.

entries.title: Share Login Details skips contacts whose portal access has been revoked
entries.summary: When sending **Share Login Details** to a group of contacts, anyone whose portal access has been revoked is now skipped and counted separately (e.g. "Sent 1 of 2") rather than receiving an email that would not work. The send summary shows each skipped contact with the reason `no_portal_access`.

where.path: Portals → [portal] → Invite people → Share Login Details

entries.use_case: When an organizer revokes a contact's portal access and then sends login details to a list that still includes that contact, the revoked contact is silently skipped — no confusing email is sent to someone who can no longer log in, and the organizer sees an accurate sent count.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that contacts who had their portal access revoked are still receiving login-detail emails.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who revokes portal access for individual contacts and then uses Share Login Details for bulk sends.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → [portal] → Invite people → Share Login Details
internal.gotchas: The skipped count appears in the send summary. Contacts are skipped only when they have no Portal_Users or Account_Users row on the event — contacts who were never granted access in the first place are also skipped.
internal.talk_track: If you revoke someone's portal access and then send login details to a group, that person is automatically skipped so they don't receive a link they can't use. The send summary shows exactly how many were sent versus skipped.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that contacts with revoked portal access are skipped when using Share Login Details, and that the send summary reflects the actual number delivered.

entries.title: Poster gallery shows correct session titles and one poster per session
entries.summary: Two bugs in the poster gallery are fixed. First, posters were displaying the uploaded file name instead of the session title; the gallery now always shows the session title. Second, when a speaker uploaded a new file into a poster slot that already had a built poster, the gallery showed two separate posters for the same session; new uploads are now saved as a version of the existing poster, so the gallery shows exactly one poster per session with the full version history accessible.
entries.use_case: Events using poster galleries were seeing file names (e.g. "poster_final_v3.pdf") as the poster title instead of the session name, and speaker re-uploads were creating duplicate poster entries. Both issues are now resolved, keeping the gallery clean and correctly labelled for attendees.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that their poster gallery shows file names instead of session titles, or that sessions appear with two posters after a speaker re-uploaded their file.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Poster Gallery beta feature.
internal.gotchas: There is one known legacy data fixture (QA session #1381) on prod-US that has two live poster roots predating this fix. A one-row SQL patch is documented in the PR but has not been applied to prod. If a customer reports a duplicate poster that predates this release, escalate for a manual data fix.
internal.talk_track: Poster galleries now always show the session title — not the file name — and when a speaker uploads a revised poster it replaces the old one as a new version rather than creating a second entry in the gallery.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that speaker re-uploads into a poster slot are saved as versions of the existing poster (not new entries), and explain how visitors can browse version history.
